scope_of_spec: GET /history and GET /history/:id route handlers: query delegation to C-4 Database Layer, response formatting, 404 and 400 error handling.
overview: The History Handler owns the two read endpoints for retrieving past check records. GET /history returns all stored check records in reverse-chronological order (most recent first). GET /history/:id returns the single record matching the given integer id, or 404 if it does not exist. Both handlers delegate all data access to C-4 (Database Layer) and are responsible only for request parsing, input validation, response formatting, and error responses. The component exports an Express Router mounted by C-1.
responsibilities: Handle GET /history by calling C-4 getAllChecks() and returning the result array as a JSON response with HTTP 200.
Handle GET /history/:id by parsing req.params.id as an integer and calling C-4 getCheckById(id).
Return HTTP 400 with { error: 'id must be a positive integer' } when req.params.id is not a valid positive integer.
Return HTTP 404 with { error: 'Check not found' } when C-4 getCheckById returns null.
Return HTTP 200 with the record object when C-4 getCheckById returns a result.
Export the handler as an Express Router.

apis.name: GET /history
apis.description: Returns all stored check records ordered by checked_at descending.

response.body_schema: Array<{ id: number, url: string, status_code: number | null, response_time_ms: number, error: string | null, checked_at: string }> — may be an empty array if no checks have been recorded

apis.name: GET /history/:id
apis.description: Returns a single check record by integer id, or 404 if not found.

response.body_schema: 200: { id: number, url: string, status_code: number | null, response_time_ms: number, error: string | null, checked_at: string } | 400: { error: string } | 404: { error: string }

behavior: GET /history: call C-4 getAllChecks(); respond HTTP 200 with the returned array (which may be []).
If parseInt result is NaN, or the parsed integer is less than 1, respond HTTP 400 { error: 'id must be a positive integer' }.
If parseInt result is a valid positive integer, call C-4 getCheckById(id).
If getCheckById returns null, respond HTTP 404 { error: 'Check not found' }.
If getCheckById returns a record, respond HTTP 200 with the record object.
edge_cases: GET /history/:id where :id is '0' or a negative number: parseInt succeeds but the value is ≤ 0. The handler must return HTTP 400, not query the database.
GET /history/:id where :id is a float string (e.g., '1.5'): parseInt('1.5', 10) returns 1 (valid integer). The handler should proceed with id=1. This is acceptable — no special case needed.
GET /history when no checks have ever been stored: C-4 getAllChecks() returns []. The handler must return HTTP 200 with an empty array [], not a 404.
GET /history/:id where :id is a valid integer but no record exists (e.g., id=9999): C-4 getCheckById returns null. The handler must return HTTP 404.
GET /history/:id where :id contains non-numeric characters (e.g., 'abc'): parseInt returns NaN. Handler returns HTTP 400.
constraints_and_considerations: This component contains zero business logic — it is a thin routing and formatting layer.
All data access is delegated to C-4; the handler must not perform any direct SQLite operations.
No pagination is implemented in this iteration. GET /history returns all records.
Records are returned in the order provided by C-4 getAllChecks() (reverse-chronological by checked_at).
The handler must not mutate or transform the fields returned by C-4 (e.g., must not reformat dates).
TypeScript strict mode: req.params.id is a string and must be explicitly parsed before use as an integer.
